overview: Warner's despatch to Grew reports the Anglo-American Direct Tea Trading Company's 1936 taxes rose sharply and late after Taihoku reclassified it from commission merchant to sales-based taxation under new regulations; the company objected to the lack of notice but accepted the new assessment.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Warner on increased taxation of an American tea company in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, American Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the reasons for, and consular discussions concerning, a threefold increase in the taxes levied on the Taiwan branch of the Anglo-American Direct Tea Trading Company.
subfiles.summary: Coughlin's tax bill, usually ¥700-800, was delayed to September 1937 and raised past ¥2,500 after Tokyo reclassified the firm from commission merchant to sales-based taxation; both sides faulted poor communication but agreed to cooperate, with Knight accepting the new basis.

interest: Shows Japanese colonial tax reclassification squeezing an American tea-trading firm in 1937 Taiwan.
